title: Tenant-aware access expiry enforcement and residency-backed audit snapshots
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Implement a tenant-scoped enforcement layer that reconciles identity lifecycles (SSO sessions, SCIM deprovision events, RBAC expiry) with tenant data residency and retention policies, and produces tamper-evident audit snapshots suitable for compliance reporting. This ticket covers: 1) enforcement of session and entitlement expiry at the routing and token validation layers; 2) a residency-aware evidence snapshot generator that combines access state, recent SCIM events, and residency tags for objects; 3) a scheduled automation that emits signed CSV/JSON artifacts and pushes metadata to the evidence pipeline and audit dashboard. The goal is to reduce manual access review effort, provide faster evidence exports for regulators, and prevent cross-region data access after a tenant's residency change or deprovisioning event.
acceptance_criteria: Access tokens and session cookies must be invalidated within 60s of an entitlement expiry or SCIM deprovision event for affected users in test tenants
Residency snapshot exports include: tenant_id, user_id, role_bindings (with effective_until), SCIM event ids, last_login, region_tag, and export_signature
Evidence artifacts are signed with the org KMS key and stored to the evidence bucket with retention metadata
Automated export job runs on schedule and has retry + backoff; failures create observable alerts in Console (runbook linked)
No functional regressions in hosted API latency >1% at p95 for unrelated traffic during rollout (validated in canary)
design_tradeoffs_and_notes: Option A (push-based invalidation) is lower-latency but increases write load across routing proxies; chosen hybrid approach: immediate push to affected nodes + eventual consistent TTL enforcement
Residency tags will be authoritative from tenant metadata service; migration will include backfilling older objects with an async job
Evidence export format favors JSONL with a CSV wrapper for auditors; signed manifest provides tamper-proofing but increases export size
We will avoid storing plaintext identities in long-term artifacts; PII is redacted per data-retention policy and replaced with stable pseudonyms where required
rollout_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests in feature branch; 2) Deploy invalidation API and snapshot generator behind feature flag to staging; 3) Canary on 5% of tenant traffic with monitoring on session invalidation and error rates; 4) Expand to Dedicated tenants with residency opt-in; 5) Full rollout with migration window and helpdesk runbook.
testing_plan: E2E tests covering SSO session lifetime override and SCIM deprovision path
Chaos test: intermittent routing node failure while invalidation messages in-flight
Compliance QA: generate signed snapshots and validate signature + manifest against KMS
Load test: simulate 10k SCIM deprovision events/hour to validate queueing and backpressure
implementation_notes: Add nullable field `residency_tag` to tenant metadata and expose in authz cache
Extend SCIM processor to emit canonical event ids to the evidence queue
Implement snapshot generator lambda that consumes tenant access state and signs outputs using HSM-backed key
Authz cache eviction hook to accept explicit invalidation events and fall back to TTL-based expiry
